builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SpecLook: Speculating Where to Look for Fast and Reliable Agentic MLLMs
summary: SpecLook replaces the sequential think-with-images loop of zoom-in tool calls in agentic MLLMs with a training-free three-level pipeline: a small model drafts a region glimpse and re-answers, the large model verifies and corrects the glimpse without tools, and only unresolved questions reach a single forward pass of the agent, skipping the iterative loop entirely. It costs an additional small-model draft inference plus fusion and verification logic, and requires serving two models or routing tiers, which adds engineering complexity even though it is training-free. It can fail when the small model's glimpse is confidently wrong yet consistent with the large model's corrected interpretation, and the claimed speedups are tied to high-resolution visual grounding benchmarks, so workloads without fine-grained image detail may see little benefit.
rationale: A training-free speculate-and-verify scheme that replaces multi-step zoom-in agent loops with small-model glimpses plus large-model verification fits constrained infrastructure and plausibly improves both latency and accuracy, but its gains depend on a suitable small drafter and the reader's workload involving high-resolution image grounding.
technique: Speculative glimpse drafting to skip zoom-in loops

claims.statement: SpecLook replaces the sequential think-with-images loop of zoom-in tool calls in agentic MLLMs with a training-free three-level pipeline: a small model drafts a region glimpse and re-answers, the large model verifies and corrects the glimpse without tools, and only unresolved questions reach a single forward pass of the agent, skipping the iterative loop entirely. It costs an additional small-model draft inference plus fusion and verification logic, and requires serving two models or routing tiers, which adds engineering complexity even though it is training-free. It can fail when the small model's glimpse is confidently wrong yet consistent with the large model's corrected interpretation, and the claimed speedups are tied to high-resolution visual grounding benchmarks, so workloads without fine-grained image detail may see little benefit.

SpecLook reaches 87.2% and 86.2% mean accuracy with 7.7x and 4.7x speedups over DeepEyes-7B and Thyme-RL agents; SpecLook-Fast reaches 9.9x and 6.3x speedups, with both variants claimed more accurate than every baseline on every split of V*, HR-Bench, and POPE.
